episodeTitle.en: How to be more innovative | Sam Schillace (Microsoft deputy CTO, creator of Google Docs)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何更具创新力 | 山姆·施利亚克（Sam Schillace，微软副首席技术官，Google Docs创始人）

guestBioOfficial.en: Sam Schillace is deputy CTO and corporate vice president at Microsoft. Prior to working at Microsoft, Sam started a company called Writely, which was acquired by Google and became the foundation of what today is Google Docs. While at Google, Sam helped lead many of Google’s consumer products, including Gmail, Blogger, PageCreator, Picasa, Reader, Groups, and more recently Maps and Google Automotive Services. Sam was also a principal investor at Google Ventures, has founded six startups, and was the SVP of engineering at Box through their IPO. In this episode, we discuss: • The journey of building Google Docs
guestBioOfficial.zh: 山姆·施利亚克是微软副首席技术官兼企业副总裁。在加入微软之前，山姆创办了名为Writely的公司，该公司被谷歌收购，并成为如今Google Docs的基础。在谷歌期间，山姆参与开发了许多消费级产品，包括Gmail、Blogger、PageCreator、Picasa、Reader、Groups，以及最近的Maps和Google Automotive Services。山姆还是Google Ventures的主要投资者，创立过六家初创公司，并在Box上市期间担任SVP工程副总裁。在本期播客中，我们将讨论：• Google Docs的开发历程

title.en: How to be more innovative | Sam Schillace (Microsoft deputy CTO, creator of Google Docs)
title.zh: 如何更具创新力 | 山姆·施利亚克（Sam Schillace，微软副首席技术官，Google Docs创始人）

summary.en: Sam shares a framework for spotting disruptive innovation: if some people love it and many hate it, it's probably disruptive, whereas broadly 'meh' reactions signal it isn't. He tells the Google Docs origin story and argues that everything around us was once a threatening disruptive idea, so we should expect new ideas to look 'dumb' at first. The conversation also covers first-principles thinking and why undervaluing what comes easily is a career trap.
summary.zh: Sam 分享了一个识别颠覆性创新的框架：如果一部分人狂热喜爱、而许多人强烈厌恶，那它很可能具有颠覆性；相反，若普遍反应平淡，则往往不是。他讲述了 Google Docs 的起源故事，并主张我们周遭的一切都曾是“令人不安的颠覆性想法”，因此应当预期新点子一开始看起来“很蠢”。对话还涉及第一性原理思维，以及为何低估“得来容易之事”是职业陷阱。
